question: Does a freshly saved Cirrove iCloud web session remain in the desktop Secret Service and restore online reads after an isolated service restart and a delayed restart?
arms: fresh sign-in, immediate separate keyring lookup and online mounted root/read
clean service stop and immediate restart, separate keyring lookup and online mounted root/read
at least 30 minutes after sign-in, clean service stop and restart, separate keyring lookup and online mounted root/read
endpoint: For each arm record only whether the exact Cirrove credential exists, whether service status is ready, root item count, and whether the previously chosen text file can be read through the mount. Do not record secret bytes, Apple bodies, cursor URLs, or file contents.
prediction: The immediate arm will pass as before; the delayed arm may reproduce the missing keyring entry seen in two private states. One pass or failure identifies a direction, not a reliable retention rate.
interpretation: At 15.2 minutes the same unlocked Secret Service item still existed but its value read as zero bytes through libsecret. The running provider remained ready from its in-memory session. After the registered 30-minute delayed restart, service and feed were sign_in_required; a mounted path alone was not evidence of online access. Earlier zero-byte lookups were incorrectly described as missing items; both older iCloud items also remain present with zero-byte values. This run fails the durable-session beta gate. One run establishes this failure, not its rate or cause.
